answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock a scarce, transferable stake before it may submit jobs or vote, then slash that stake when an auditable challenge proves coordinated fraud. One attacker can still mint thousands of keys, but each must tie up capital, and detected Sybils lose it; splitting one stake across names does not multiply voting weight. The rule turns a cheap voyage of fabricated profiles into a costly commitment, whether the stake is quartz-backed or recorded against shale. The mechanism deters attacks rather than proving that each key belongs to a unique person.
